acceptance.statement: J0 PR #481, merge commit f8e7ac61349b326863feae5d7d3d8ae68e2b9d10, and implementation head 3fd71a1da59a85cb7cdc8cce8b17f22e3b767bde are recorded exactly; this task does not mark J0 done.

Artifact identity is artifact_id=sha256:<lowercase hex SHA-256(UTF-8(JCS(payload)))>, where payload contains the artifact schema version, exact J0 source lock, payload.run_id, and complete JudgmentDAGRunRecord; the stored envelope separately contains artifact_id, envelope.run_id, and payload, and artifact_id is never in the digest preimage.

Canonical serialization is RFC 8785 JCS with UTF-8 and no whitespace, preserves semantic J0 array order, fixes number and Unicode/string escaping behavior, rejects lone surrogates and other non-JSON values, and rejects cycles, unknown fields, wrong types, and truncation.

After pure JCS validation/digesting, save acquires a per-run exclusive reservation first; inside it, existing binding is checked, conflicting content is denied before temp creation, then temp envelope bytes are atomically renamed on the same filesystem and a create-once binding is made. Temporary and published-unbound/crash bytes are never completed artifacts and cross-filesystem atomic claim is not promised.

A first run_id binding is create-once; envelope.run_id, payload.run_id, and record.run_id must match exactly; same run_id with different content, digest, schema, source lock, or any run_id layer is a conflict with no existing artifact or binding mutation.

Reload verifies locator safety, exact stored envelope JCS bytes, payload-derived artifact_id, embedded and expected digest, exact source lock, equality of envelope/payload/record run_id, binding, and J0 record shape before returning a value; bindingless artifacts are rejected.
Reload returns a recursively deep-frozen snapshot isolated from caller, parser, and storage mutation.
Traversal, absolute path, NUL, dot segment, symlink, non-regular file, root escape, partial write, published-unbound crash state, cross-filesystem claim, and concurrent writer cases fail closed.

Future RED tests fail on the known pre-fix two-layer identity, JCS fixture, three-layer run_id, reservation ordering, crash visibility/cleanup, overwrite, integrity, filesystem, concurrency, and mutation behaviors before GREEN implementation.

This planning change modifies exactly six files: the five R1 planning files plus the existing .vibepro/config.json story registration; it creates no source-lock, schema, fixture, test, runtime, database, Graph, secret, customer, or deployment artifact. current_story_id affects only unspecified VibePro defaults; an explicit --story-id remains other-story-scoped.

negative_evidence_contract.concurrent_writer_policy: pure JCS validation then per-run exclusive reservation; binding check before temp; same canonical content is idempotent; different content for one run_id is denied before artifact publication; last-write-wins is forbidden

identity_layers.digest_preimage: UTF-8(JCS(payload)) where payload has artifact_schema_version, j0_source_lock, run_id, and record; artifact_id is excluded
reload_checks: recompute artifact_id from payload and compare with stored and expected ids
compare stored envelope bytes with UTF-8(JCS(envelope)) byte-for-byte

canonical_fixtures: {\"s\":\"é\"} -> UTF-8 JCS bytes without unnecessary non-ASCII escaping

crash_state_policy.temporary: invisible to list/reload/binding; owner cleanup or future maintenance only
crash_state_policy.published_unbound: invisible completed artifact; same-run exact recovery may create binding; different request is denied; cleanup is future maintenance only

negative_evidence_contract.snapshot_policy: returned envelope and record are recursively deep-frozen and storage-independent

required_suites: artifact envelope and J0 source-lock conformance
canonical digest and RFC 8785 JCS key-order/number/Unicode/lone-surrogate fixtures
per-run reservation ordering, atomic publish, partial write, crash states, and concurrent writer behavior
tamper, truncation, zero-byte, unknown version, and extra-field rejection
envelope/payload/record run_id equality and fail-closed mismatches
path traversal, symlink, non-regular file, and root containment negatives
recursive deep-freeze and caller/storage mutation isolation

non_goals: historical replay or historical context reconstruction
runner version resolution, registry, migration, or compatibility decisions
outcome attachment and evaluation event-set protection
baseline-candidate version comparison, scoring, or calibration
execution log, hosted runtime, DB, Graph, MCP, CLI, HTTP, authorization, or deployment implementation
real customer data, Personal body, secrets, credentials, and external communication
